title: AWS, Google Cloud and Azure: equivalent services

videos.script: Every provider sells the same building blocks. {{blocks}} The cloud course already translated their names. This lesson asks a defender's question instead. How far does one grant reach? And what is true before anybody configures anything? {{hierarchy}} At Google Cloud and Azure, a role given high up flows down to everything below it. At AWS, a grant stays in its own account. Guardrails flow down at all three. {{everybody}} Each provider has a way to say everybody. And each has one that sounds narrower than it is. Authenticated never means ours. {{defaults}} The defaults differ too. Google Cloud's default network lets SSH in from anywhere. And at all three, nobody records who read a file unless somebody asked beforehand. {{control}} Then one sentence becomes three mechanisms. No patient file is ever public. You will write the AWS half in your lab, and read the other two. {{end}}
